title: NIGHTFORM night-drive drop: pull six beats from one 4K take, neutralize each to its in-frame grey card and build one authored night-look, then data-merge a designed cover-card board plus a vertical sizzle reel
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a short-form vertical-video creator who wanted a freelance editor to turn raw night footage into a post-ready package with 'on-brand colour, a scroll-stopping cover, and captions' for the vertical short-video feeds. Laundered to a fictional creator brand, 'NIGHTFORM' (handle @nightform), with the real platform names replaced by generic 'vertical short-video feeds' / 'the vertical feed' and every craft app named only in generic terms (colour-grade / authored cover-card template / timeline finish) — no real person, company, product, marketplace, app or trademark is named in any task-facing field. STRENGTHENED from the killed original, which (a) counted upload init/finalize pairs as work and pasted one filter recipe onto a single hero still, (b) fed video_create_quick_cut THREE short AI clips as an 'assembly' (quick_cut can only SHORTEN one longer take, never assemble or lengthen), and (c) shipped a thumbnail whose spec claimed the wordmark was already 'locked up in the corner' while the workflow left the compositing to a human (the connector cannot composite). The corrected design keeps the exact job the brief rewards — a post-ready night-drive short-form PACKAGE — but routes it to what the connectors genuinely do and buys its difficulty from DEPTH: the creator shot ONE continuous ~45s 4K night-drive take, and an 18% grey card is clipped to the dashboard edge in frame for the whole take. The freelancer PULLS six strong beats from that one take (a creative selection the agent owns — which beat, which sharp frame), and because the take rolls through wildly mixed, drifting street light (warm dashboard tungsten, cool sodium-vapour underpass, saturated neon signage, orange street-light pools on wet asphalt) no two pulled beats match out of the file. Each beat must be neutralized to its OWN in-frame grey card so the six converge on one common white point, THEN carried onto one agent-authored 'night-look' built from primitives (a cool, crushed-black split feel with the street-light hues settled back and the neon accent lifted — reasoned, not a canned preset). The graded covers data-merge into a genuinely hand-authored single-record cover-card template (the wordmark reaches the corner lockup ONLY through a second @image merge column, never by hand-compositing), producing a designed cover board the agent owns, plus a same-take vertical sizzle reel and a captions cue-sheet asset. Nothing beyond the brief's own 'colour, cover, captions, vertical cut' is invented.
one_line_ask: Pull six strong beats from NIGHTFORM's single ~45s 4K night-drive take, neutralize each pulled frame to the 18% grey card that stays in the take so the whole set reads as one grade (each beat needs its own white-balance and exposure decision because the street light drifts across the take), carry them onto one agent-authored night-look, crop each to the vertical cover window without upscaling, vectorize the wordmark, then data-merge the creator's authored single-record cover-card template into one designed cover per row — plus a ~15s vertical sizzle reel cut from the same take and a captions cue-sheet asset.
full_brief:
I run @nightform, a fast-growing vertical short-video account, and I need one night-drive shoot turned into a post-ready drop package. I am NOT looking for a finished timeline film here — my editor does the final cut, the caption burn-in and any motion graphics on the timeline. What I need from you is the colour and cover package built off the ONE take we already shot.

Here is what you get: (1) nightdrive_take_4k.mp4 — a single continuous ~45 second 4K night-drive take, hand-held-steady from inside the car: pulling away from a lit kerb, rolling under a concrete underpass, stopped at a lit crossing, out across a wet open stretch, past a strip of neon storefronts, and finally around a lamp-lit off-ramp. Because it is one long take through changing street light, different moments do NOT match each other straight out of the file — some are warm and dim, some go cold and murky, some are blown out with neon. To make the match checkable we clipped an 18% grey card to the dashboard at the edge of frame and it stays in shot the whole take. (2) coverboard_template.indd — the cover-card page we hand-built, one card per page, with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (the full-bleed cover and the corner wordmark lockup). (3) cover_shotlist.csv — our six-beat list: the beat name, a framing note, a run label and a format tag per card. (4) nightform_wordmark_flat.png — our flat wordmark on transparency, which we want razor-sharp in the corner of every cover. (5) captions_script.json — a short caption cue-sheet.

What I need back:
- THE COVER BOARD (the deliverable I care about most): a designed cover board, ONE cover card per beat, six cards, that I review and post from. For each of the six beats, pull the strongest, SHARP frame near that beat out of the take (if the beat lands on a motion-blurred moment, step to the clean frame beside it — a soft cover reads cheap and I will reject it), grade it, drop it full-bleed into the card with its beat name, run label and my @nightform handle bound in from the list, and my wordmark crisp in the corner lockup. The cover has to look art-directed, not like a filter dropped on a screenshot.
- THE GRADE (this is the whole craft of it): the six cards have to read as ONE drop, not six frames from six different nights. First bring every pulled frame to the SAME neutral base — the grey card in that frame has to land truly neutral (no leftover warm or cold cast) at one common white point, and the set has to share one exposure feel. Because the take's light drifts, no two beats start from the same cast or brightness, so getting all six onto that one white point is a per-frame decision — each frame gets neutralized to its OWN in-frame grey card, and how far and which way to move is yours to judge from that card, frame by frame. A set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will drift apart at the grey cards and I will reject it. THEN put them all onto one night-look I can call mine: cool and moody with the blacks set deep, the harsh street-light colours settled back so they don't fight the mood, and the neon accent given a controlled lift — one look, built to my brand, applied so all six covers feel like one release. Judge the look per frame too: a frame swamped by one street-light colour needs a heavier hand than one already close, or the set won't match. When you are done, hand back, per frame, the white-balance (temperature / tint) and exposure move you dialed and the final pixel size, so I can confirm the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed.
- COVER SIZE: each cover card is a 1080 x 1920 vertical, and the cover image behind it needs to fill that at full 1080 x 1920 from real pixels — the take is 4K, so a vertical crop from the full frame clears it; a cover graded on a small proxy, or a landscape frame stretched to fill vertical, will fall under and post soft. Do not enlarge past what the 4K frame holds.
- THE REEL: a ~15 second vertical (1080x1920) sizzle cut from the SAME take for the drop — shortened from the long take (no lengthening, no stitching in other clips) and reframed to vertical, no upscaling (the 4K master has the height for it). Frame-accurate timeline cuts, transitions, motion graphics and burned-in captions are my editor's timeline finish, not part of this pass.
- THE WORDMARK: my flat wordmark cleaned to a crisp vector for the corner lockup and reusable on future covers.
- THE CAPTIONS: my caption cue-sheet finalized into the project folder as a data asset for my editor to burn on during the timeline finish — I know the automated pass doesn't paint text onto the video.

Keep the sources in my cloud project folder. Bind the beat names, run labels and my handle verbatim from the list — do not rename my beats. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the six covers matched to one white point and one night-look with the per-frame moves reported; every cover image at least 1080 x 1920 real pixels; the reel a shortened vertical cut of the one take at 1080x1920, same-or-shorter runtime, never upscaled; the wordmark a crisp vector in every corner lockup; and exactly one cover card per list row.

inputs.name: nightdrive_take_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CAMERA ORIGINAL (declared at camera scale; no generative video model produces this length/resolution reliably, which is the point — it must be a real capture): a single continuous ~45 second 4K (3840x2160, 16:9, ~24-30fps) hand-held-steady night-drive take shot from inside a car, candid documentary look, real rolling-shutter wobble, headlight bloom and compression noise in the shadows, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions, and NO real brand names, logos, badges, dashboard-screen content, sign text or trademarks on any object (dashboard screen dark/blank, all neon signage abstract non-readable glyphs, unbranded or fictional only). Across the ONE take the street light drifts hard so the pulled beats will NOT match each other: (~00:04) pulling away from a lit kerb, cabin lit by warm tungsten dashboard glow, dark surround — WARM and DIM; (~00:11) rolling under a concrete underpass in cold sodium-vapour / mercury fill — COOL, blue-green, UNDEREXPOSED and murky; (~00:19) stopped at a lit crossing with mixed traffic-signal glow and a magenta neon store sign filling the windshield — fairly BRIGHT, MAGENTA-dominant, slightly cool; (~00:27) out across a wet open stretch with orange street-lamp pools streaking on the wet asphalt, little else lit — LOW-KEY, ORANGE-dominant, warm; (~00:34) tracking past a strip of saturated magenta-and-cyan neon storefronts — BRIGHT, very HIGH-SATURATION mixed neon; (~00:41) around a lamp-lit off-ramp curve under a flood of sodium-orange street lamps — MID brightness, strong ORANGE cast. An 18% grey card is clipped to the dashboard at the FAR EDGE of frame and stays visible in shot for the entire take as a white-balance reference. Real handheld drift, shallow depth in the tighter beats, wet-road reflections.
inputs.realism_notes: TRAP + PER-FRAME DIAGNOSIS LIVE HERE (not in the brief, csv or step notes). ONE genuine ~45s 4K camera take, declared at camera scale so both downstream needs are honest: (a) frames pulled with video_render_frame are native 3840x2160 stills, so a vertical 1080x1920 cover crop from the FULL frame (the 9:16 strip of a 3840x2160 frame is ~1215x2160) clears the 1080x1920 floor as a DOWNSCALE, never an upscale; (b) video_create_quick_cut shortens the ~45s take to a ~15s sizzle (output shorter than source — never a lengthen or a multi-clip assembly), and video_resize reframes that 4K 16:9 cut to a same-length 1080x1920 vertical (the 4K height carries the 9:16 strip so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale — a 1080p source could NOT deliver it). The light deliberately drifts across the single take so the six pulled beats start from DIFFERENT casts and exposures and cannot be matched with one blanket correction: beat 1 (kerb) warm+dim, beat 2 (underpass) cold+murky+underexposed, beat 3 (crossing) magenta-dominant+bright, beat 4 (wet stretch) orange-dominant+low-key, beat 5 (storefronts) very high-saturation mixed neon+bright, beat 6 (off-ramp) strong orange+mid. THE TRAP the brief does NOT disclose (it states only 'read as one drop'): the naive path applies ONE global white-balance/look to every frame, or auto-tones each frame to look fine on its own — both leave the grey cards disagreeing (warm and cold beats drift apart) and the covers read as six different nights; a second naive path tries to force the phonk teal/magenta by ROTATING the orange sodium light all the way to teal, which is a near-complementary hue rotation the recolor tool cannot do controllably (>~90 degrees is out of reach) — the connector-correct move is to neutralize to the card, then DESATURATE-AND-DARKEN the orange street-light band toward gunmetal and LIFT the already-present magenta neon, letting the cool balance + crushed blacks carry the night-look; a third pitfall is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference) or grading on a downscaled proxy (falling under the 1080x1920 cover floor). The grey card stays in shot throughout so every pulled frame carries the reference; it is cropped OUT of the delivered covers but RETAINED in the neutralized masters for the grade audit. The ~45s runtime is longer than any target derived from it (six stills; a ~15s shortened cut) and the take is a real capture, not an ~8s AI clip.

inputs.name: coverboard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built layout-engine document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 1080 x 1920 px portrait (9:16) vertical cover card — ONE card per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<ShotNo>>, <<Beat>>, <<Handle>>, <<RunLabel>>, <<FormatTag>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a full-bleed 1080 x 1920 cover frame bound to @Cover (the graded pulled frame for that beat), and a small corner wordmark-lockup frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned and the connector cannot composite, the wordmark reaches the corner lockup ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The <<Beat>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long beat name binds without going overset. The card furniture (a lower title bar, a hairline grid, the handle line, the safe-area margins) is already drawn into the template and is fixed on every card, so the only per-row imagery is the cover frame and the corner wordmark. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up contact sheet: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-record-per-page sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-cover-per-page board is the correct, connector-doable shape (six rows => a six-page board), not a multi-up contact sheet. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@Cover, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded cover AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path into every corner lockup WITHOUT any free-form placement or compositing (this is the correction of the killed original's over-claim that the wordmark was already 'locked up in the corner'). Column names must exactly match the shot-list headers. The 1080x1920 card is a screen/vertical-cover canvas exported whole by document_render_layout; the hero is simply page one.

inputs.name: cover_shotlist.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: ShotNo,Beat,Handle,RunLabel,FormatTag,@Cover,@Wordmark and 6 rows, one per requested cover beat, in take order. ShotNo is 01..06. Beat is the human beat name and MUST include at least one deliberately LONG name (e.g. 'Storefront Strip — Neon Mile at the Crawl', ~40+ chars) alongside short ones (e.g. 'Kerb Pull', 'Underpass', 'The Crossing', 'Wet Mile', 'Off-Ramp') so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. Handle is '@nightform' on every row (bound verbatim). RunLabel is a short client label string per card ('DROP 01' .. 'DROP 06'). FormatTag is one of exactly two values: 'Feed Cover' or 'Story Cover'. IMPORTANT: no column may name a lighting cast, colour temperature, exposure, warm/cool direction, saturation or any grade/treatment — the Beat and any framing sense must describe only the beat/place, so the correction direction stays the freelancer's decision judged from the grey card, never a value read off the CSV; and no column may encode the treatment via a file-type or a .ext hint. @Cover holds the agreed prepped cover filename for that beat (cover_01_final.jpg .. cover_06_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded cover into that card. @Wordmark holds 'nightform_wordmark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized lockup binds onto every card). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<ShotNo>>,<<Beat>>,<<Handle>>,<<RunLabel>>,<<FormatTag>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six cover cards (page-count = row-count gate). The @Cover column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned lockup lands on every card. Handle/RunLabel/Beat are client copy bound verbatim. Deliberately NON-DIAGNOSTIC: no lighting/temperature/treatment column and no file-type hint, so the CSV cannot tell the agent which frame is warm vs cold vs neon-swamped — the agent must decide each correction from the grey card and the frame's content. The long storefront beat exercises the auto-fit name frame.

inputs.name: nightform_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat minimalist creator wordmark on a TRANSPARENT background: the single word 'NIGHTFORM' in a tight geometric condensed sans-serif, solid single-colour (pure white) glyphs, crisp clean hard edges, high contrast, centred with a generous transparent margin all around, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, exported slightly oversized and off-centre, 2400x600 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, single-colour text art on transparent alpha so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds to strip the generous transparent margin, then a crisp contrast pass so the edges separate hard). Text-bearing wordmark -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms. It is a SUPPLIED asset only cleaned and vectorized, never a from-scratch designed letterform. White glyphs on transparent alpha vectorize cleanly and read on the dark cover; enclosed counters (the O, the A, the R, the G) sit on transparency so no dark-ground enclosed-counter knockout is claimed.

inputs.name: captions_script.json
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a small JSON array of 6 caption cues for a ~15s vertical night-drive reel, each cue an object with fields {index, start_seconds, end_seconds, text}: short punchy all-caps on-screen lines under 24 characters each, matching a moody late-night driving mood, no real brand names or hashtags. Structure only — this is a cue-sheet the editor burns onto the video during the timeline finish; it is NOT rendered onto frames by the connector.
inputs.realism_notes: Realistic caption cue-sheet the creator's editor burns on during the manual timeline finish; delivered as an uploaded JSON data asset, giving a concrete captions deliverable without claiming the connector can paint text onto video frames.

outputs.name: NIGHTFORM_CoverBoard_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED DELIVERABLE. A designed cover board exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge: ONE cover card per beat, SIX pages (page-count = shot-list row-count = 6), each a 1080 x 1920 portrait card that binds its ShotNo/Beat/Handle/RunLabel/FormatTag verbatim from the list, drops that beat's grey-card-neutralized, house-night-look cover full-bleed into the @Cover frame (filled at >=1080x1920 real pixels), and drops the vectorized wordmark into the corner @Wordmark lockup. The board reads as one continuous grade and one authored night-look across all six cards. The 'hero' is simply page one of the merged board (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the authored cool/crushed night-look, the beat selection, the crisp lockup, the art-directed card — is the agent's, not a template default or a canned filter.

outputs.name: phonk_reel_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: A ~15s vertical (1080x1920) sizzle reel cut from the SAME single take: video_create_quick_cut shortens the ~45s 4K take to a ~15s highlight (output shorter than source — no lengthening, no multi-clip assembly), then video_resize reframes that cut to a same-length 1080x1920 vertical (an honest downscale from the 4K height, never an upscale). ~15s is a best-effort target since quick_cut/resize are [A] async product actions whose exact final duration is widget-polled, not fully headless-retrievable. Frame-accurate timeline cuts, transitions, motion graphics and burned-in captions are the creator's editor's manual timeline finish and are NOT part of this automated deliverable.

outputs.name: reel_captions.json
outputs.spec: The on-screen captions asset: a JSON cue-sheet of 6 caption cues, each {index, start_seconds, end_seconds, text} in short all-caps night-drive lines (<24 chars), finalized into the creator's cloud project folder. Delivered as an uploaded data asset for the editor to burn onto the video during the manual finish — the connector does not paint text onto video frames.

outputs.name: cover_masters_cardbearing_x6
outputs.spec: Six grey-card-neutralized full-frame masters (native ~3840x2160), one per pulled beat, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven to a clean neutral and the whole set matched to one shared white point and exposure feel — captured BEFORE the night-look is applied, with the grey card RETAINED in frame. This is the grade-audit artifact the grader checks neutrality on (the card is cropped out of the delivered covers, so neutrality is graded here, on the retained card-bearing masters, not on the look-graded covers). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each frame.

outputs.name: cover_frames_x6
outputs.spec: Six vertical covers (cover_01_final.jpg .. cover_06_final.jpg), each derived from the retained card-bearing master by applying the shared agent-authored night-look (cool balance, deep blacks, street-light hues settled back, neon accent lifted — dialed per frame so the set matches) and then cropping the grey card OUT and reframing to the 1080 x 1920 (9:16) cover window from the FULL-resolution frame, held at >=1080x1920 real pixels (never upscaled). These are the @Cover assets the merge resolves per row; card-exclusion is checked here separately from the neutrality check on the masters.

outputs.name: nightform_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat wordmark cleaned and vectorized to a crisp SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds then a crisp contrast pass then trace), razor-sharp at any size, bound into every cover's corner lockup via the @Wordmark column and reusable on future covers.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (NOT the primary output; the cover board is): for each of the six pulled beats, the white-balance temperature and tint and the exposure move applied to neutralize it, the per-frame hue/tone moves dialed to seat it on the shared night-look, plus the final pixel size of each cover, plus the single common white point all six were matched to. This makes 'the set is matched to one target and one look' checkable — the corrections must be non-identical across the warm-dim, cold-murky and neon-swamped beats. It is an applied-settings log, never a measured/recovered pixel readout.

Finalize the take upload from step 1 into a real cloud video assetId with a fetchable URL — the single source for both the pulled cover frames and the vertical sizzle reel.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining anchored on the one client take. VIDEO/GRADE SPINE: the 4K take is uploaded (1) and finalized (2 -> take_asset); video_metadata (3) reads its duration/format so the six beats sample across the real ~45s. Six video_render_frame pulls (4-9) each pull a DIFFERENT beat from take_asset (the creative selection the agent owns — which beat, which sharp frame), yielding native 3840x2160 stills frame_01_raw..frame_06_raw. Each raw frame drives its own three-step grade sub-chain: image_apply_adjustments neutralization to the in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per beat — 10,14,18,22,26,30 — whose output is the RETAINED card-bearing master), then image_apply_adjustments tonal night-look base (11,15,19,23,27,31), then image_adjust_hsl authored hue signature (12,16,20,24,28,32), then image_crop_and_resize (13,17,21,25,29,33) that crops the grey card OUT and reframes to the 1080x1920 cover window from the FULL frame at >=1080x1920 px. Every neutralization is driven to that frame's own grey card so all six converge on one shared white point, then onto one authored look. video_create_quick_cut (34) shortens take_asset to a ~15s sizzle and video_resize (35) reframes it to the same-length 1080x1920 vertical reel. WORDMARK BRANCH: upload-init (36) -> finalize (37 -> wordmark_asset) -> crop_to_bounds (38) -> crisp adjustments (39) -> image_vectorize (40 -> nightform_wordmark.svg). CAPTIONS: upload-init (41) -> finalize (42 -> reel_captions.json data asset). CONVERGENCE: the six covers and the vectorized wordmark fan into the merge upload session (43) -> finalize (44 -> merge_asset_urns) -> document_merge_data_layout (45), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the shot-list CSV and emits one cover card per row resolving BOTH @Cover and @Wordmark; the merged set exports to the cover-board PDF (46). The only non-chained calls are the four standard upload-init idioms (1,36,41,43), each immediately consumed by its finalize; everything else sets inputs_from to a producing step's output.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 46 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (video [A] frame-pull/quick-cut/reframe + [C] metadata, image raster [C], layout merge [T]/[C]) — well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the four upload idioms (8 plumbing calls), leaving 38 difficulty-bearing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: the core is six DIFFERENT reasoned grade decisions, in different directions, all forced to converge on one measurable target (the static in-frame 18% grey card) and then onto one agent-authored night-look, even though the six beats were pulled from a single take whose light drifts hard — a warm-dim kerb pull, a cold-murky underexposed underpass, a magenta-swamped crossing, an orange-pooled wet stretch, a high-saturation neon strip, a strong-orange off-ramp — so a blanket batch correction or per-frame auto-tone visibly fails to match at the grey cards. The authored look is itself connector-constraint reasoning: the phonk teal/magenta cannot be forced by a near-complementary hue ROTATION (the recolor tool cannot swing orange to teal past ~90 degrees), so the agent must reason to a build-from-primitives look — neutralize to the card, cool the balance and crush the blacks, DESATURATE-AND-DARKEN the street-light band toward gunmetal and LIFT the already-present magenta neon — dialed per frame so a neon-swamped beat is restrained and a near-neutral beat is pushed, or the set drifts apart. Layered on top: camera-scale reasoning (a 1080x1920 vertical cover can only be met by cropping the 9:16 strip from the FULL 3840x2160 frame — grading on a proxy or stretching falls under the floor, and no upscaling is permitted anywhere; the same reasoning makes the video_resize reel honest only because the source is 4K), prep-before-trace wordmark discipline (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> vectorize), and a two-image-column one-file-per-row merge into a hand-authored single-record template that also fixes the killed original's over-claim by routing the wordmark to the corner ONLY through an @image bind. Respects every hard limit: video_render_frame pulls native stills (no upscale); video_create_quick_cut SHORTENS one longer take (no assembly, no lengthen); video_resize is a same-length reframe of the 4K cut (no trim, no upscale); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; no generative fill/expand/text-to-image/object-removal/from-scratch art; no image_fill_area, no image_apply_color_overlay; HSL stays within bounded per-band moves (no >90-degree rotation); auto-tone is the named trap, not a step; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used and the merge places one record per page (no N-up). Deprecated tools (image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast) are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the six cover cards must read as ONE drop — every pulled frame's in-frame 18% grey card driven to one common white point with the set on one exposure feel, then all six carried onto one agent-authored night-look — and because the beats were pulled from a single take whose light drifts, each needs its OWN correction (warm-dim, cold-murky and neon-swamped beats move in different directions and by different amounts); running one global white-balance/look, or per-frame auto-tone (which keys off each frame's own histogram), leaves the beats disagreeing at the grey cards and the board is rejected. The agent must REPORT the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure and the per-frame look moves and final pixel size so 'matched' is auditable rather than asserted. Two further checkable gates back it: every cover must fill at >=1080x1920 real pixels (cropped from the full 4K frame, never upscaled) and the merged PDF page-count must equal the shot-list row-count (6), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable common white point across six frames pulled from one changing-light take, each requiring a different, sometimes opposite correction reasoned to its own retained grey card, then a shared authored look dialed per frame — not one set of sliders; (2) constraint-reasoning around a tool limitation — the phonk teal/magenta look CANNOT be produced by a near-complementary HSL rotation of the orange street light (>~90 degrees is out of reach and uncontrollable), so it must be built from primitives (neutralize + cool + crushed blacks + desaturate-and-darken the street-light band toward gunmetal + lift the existing magenta neon); plus the vertical cover can only come from cropping the 9:16 strip of the FULL 4K frame with no upscaling, and prep-before-trace wordmark discipline. TRAP (the brief does NOT disclose it — it states only the goal 'read as one drop' and leaves the method to the agent; the diagnosis lives in the take's realism_notes): the naive path applies one global correction or auto-tones each pulled frame so each looks fine alone, which passes a thumbnail glance but drifts apart at the grey cards and fails the one-white-point gate; a second is trying to rotate the orange light all the way to teal (impossible/uncontrollable) instead of the neutralize-then-settle-and-lift build; a third is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference) — which is why neutrality is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing masters and card-exclusion is checked separately on the covers; a fourth is grading on a downscaled proxy or stretching a landscape frame to fill vertical, dropping under the 1080x1920 floor. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, agent never measures): every grey card neutral (R=G=B) at the common white point on the six retained card-bearing masters with per-frame WB/exposure reported; every cover >=1080x1920 real px with final px reported; the reel a shortened 1080x1920 vertical cut of the one take (same-or-shorter runtime, never upscaled); the wordmark a crisp vector in every corner lockup; and exactly one cover card per shot-list row in the exported board.
